beliefs.label: Protect Closeness
beliefs.statement: I protect closeness by making room before I ask for it

receipts.quote: Theo came home tired, so I made tea and waited beside him before mentioning our rent increase. I wanted the evening to have room for him first.
At my friend's birthday, I asked about her new job before telling everyone I had lost a client. My news could wait for a quieter moment.

beliefs.label: Being Understood
beliefs.statement: Being understood matters more to me than winning an argument

receipts.quote: Theo and I disagreed about the kitchen shelves, and I said I wanted him to understand why the height mattered to me. We measured together afterward.
My supervisor wanted a brighter label, but I explained how glare hid the artifact's detail. She changed the light instead.

beliefs.label: Carry Uncertainty
beliefs.statement: I can carry uncertainty without filling every silence

receipts.quote: The museum delayed its contract decision for a week. I worked on another display instead of sending three follow-up emails.
Theo's train was late and his phone battery died. I read at the cafe until he arrived rather than imagining reasons.

beliefs.label: Good Work
beliefs.statement: Good work needs time to notice what the first draft misses

receipts.quote: I asked to keep the cracked enamel cup in the exhibit because its repair showed how it had been used. The team looked closer.
Before finalizing wall text, I watched three visitors search for the entrance. We moved the opening panel after lunch.

beliefs.label: Hear Care
beliefs.statement: I hear care in questions that leave me room to answer

receipts.quote: Theo asked if I wanted help or company after a difficult client call. I could answer without defending why I was upset.
My sister asked what kind of birthday dinner I wanted, then waited while I chose. I told her the truth.

beliefs.label: Soften Hard
beliefs.statement: I soften a hard point until it risks disappearing

receipts.quote: When Theo left dishes beside the sink, I said the kitchen felt crowded rather than saying I was angry. He did not know what I meant.
My manager moved my deadline, and I said it was fine even though it cut our research time. I rewrote the schedule later.

beliefs.label: Shared Space
beliefs.statement: A shared space works when both people can leave their mark on it

receipts.quote: Theo wanted his grandmother's lamp in the living room, and I wanted my broad chair by the window. We shifted both until the room held them.
We hung his concert posters beside my framed maps instead of choosing one wall's owner. The hallway looked like both of us.

beliefs.label: Objects Become
beliefs.statement: Objects become meaningful when someone tells the ordinary story around them

receipts.quote: An old lunch pail came with no label, so I asked the donor about packed sandwiches and factory shifts. Her answer gave it a life.
I placed a faded bus pass beside a recording of its owner's first commute. Visitors stopped longer at that case.

shared_items.label: How I mean things
shared_items.statement: I circle toward a difficult point before I can name it.

shared_items.label: What feels like care
shared_items.statement: A patient question makes me feel invited rather than managed.

shared_items.label: How to bring something up with me
shared_items.statement: Ask gently and leave enough quiet for the real answer.
